描述_EN: this bottle is an example of cizhou ware, a type of ceramic made in the northern part of china during the song dynasty (960-1279). cizhou wares were utilitarian at their time of production and were made in relatively large numbers. however, some of these 'prunus vases' are inscribed with the chinese words 'fine wine'. although they were not given high praise at the time of production, the bold designs and simple shapes of cizhou wares were later treasured by japanese and western connoisseurs alike. the studio pottery movement in britain found affinity with ceramics like this vase, which bernard leach praised in his seminal publication, a potter’s book, in 1940. this bottle is made in a shape known as meiping (prunus vase), but it was most likely used to store alcohol. the term cizhou encapsulates a range of wares made in several regions of northern china, often consisting of a course stoneware body covered with a white slip (a thin layer of diluted firing clay), and then decorated with a contrasting colour. vessels of this shape have traditionally been referred to as meiping, literally 'prunus vases'.
描述_ZN: 本壺是中國北方宋代(960-1279)製造的一種陶器--慈禧瓷器的例子。 慈溪器皿在生产时是功利性的，而且制作数量相对较多。 然而，这些'梅花瓶'中的一些刻有中文'美酒'二字。 虽然在生产的时候没有得到很高的评价，但是慈禧的大胆设计和简单的造型后来被日本和西方的鉴赏家们所珍视。 英国的工作室陶艺运动发现了像这个花瓶这样的陶瓷的亲和力，伯纳德-利奇在1940年的开创性出版物《陶艺家之书》中称赞了这个花瓶。 这个瓶子的形状被称为梅瓶，但它很可能是用来储存酒精的。 这个术语概括了中国北方几个地区制造的一系列器物，通常由白滑（一层薄薄的稀释的烧制粘土）覆盖的石器主体组成，然后用对比的颜色进行装饰。 这种形状的器皿传统上被称为梅瓶，字面意思是 "梅花瓶"。
